# Structured goldens that do not have a raw byte file yet.
# Move a name out of this list in the same change that adds raw/<name>.http.
# /api/status and every non-200 goldenCases entry must be raw, not pending.
#
# A raw file is the exact Python _json_response or _no_content byte string.
# Compare status, reason, body, and every header except Date. Do not sort
# keys, re-encode numbers, or drop fields. Optional raw/<name>.paths lists
# JSON Pointers; only those value spans may be replaced, and a missing path
# fails. Content-Length is the body length from before that replacement.
# Set-Cookie order, Cache-Control, and WWW-Authenticate are compared.
#
# Not in this list, and not served by the Go server yet:
# raw/no-content.http is the OPTIONS 204 shape (fixture only).
# 401 WWW-Authenticate, sign-in Set-Cookie / Cache-Control, 413, a bad
# request line, and a bad Content-Length are later cards.
# Static 405 Allow is Go-only and is not a Python raw case.
# The semicolon parity case reuses task-rich.json and is still structured only.
